question: A coordinator has several custom subagents defined, each with a description field summarizing what it's for. When a new query arrives, the coordinator does not explicitly name any subagent. How does it typically decide which, if any, subagent to invoke?
options: A) It requires the query to include the subagent's exact name, otherwise no subagent is ever considered for delegation
B) It always invokes every defined subagent and discards the ones whose output isn't relevant to the query
C) It invokes subagents in the fixed order they were defined in the agents configuration, regardless of the query
D) It matches the query against each subagent's description field and delegates automatically when a match is found
correct_answers: D) It matches the query against each subagent's description field and delegates automatically when a match is found
explanations: Explicit naming is one way to guarantee a specific subagent is used, but it is not required; automatic delegation based on description matching works without naming a subagent.
Invoking every subagent regardless of relevance wastes effort and contradicts the coordinator's role in dynamically selecting which subagents a query actually needs.
Definition order in the agents configuration has no bearing on invocation; matching is based on the description field's relevance to the query, not declaration sequence.
Correct. Claude determines whether to invoke a subagent based on how well the query matches that subagent's description field, delegating automatically without requiring an explicit name.
